questions.enonce_markdown:
Briefly explain the following terms:

(a) MODEM. (2 marks)

(b) Firewall. (2 marks)

(c) Router. (2 marks)
questions.corrige_markdown:
**(a) MODEM (2 marks).** The word comes from **MO**dulator-**DEM**odulator. A modem converts the *digital* signals produced by a computer into *analogue* signals that can travel over a telephone line or a cable (modulation), and converts the incoming analogue signals back into digital data that the computer can use (demodulation). It is the device that connects a computer or a LAN to an Internet Service Provider (for example an ADSL modem on a telephone line).

**(b) Firewall (2 marks).** A firewall is a piece of hardware or software placed between a private network (or a computer) and an outside network such as the Internet. It examines every incoming and outgoing packet and allows or blocks it according to a set of security rules (addresses, ports, protocols). It therefore prevents unauthorised access, hackers and some malware from entering the network.

**(c) Router (2 marks).** A router is a network device that connects two or more different networks (for example a school LAN and the Internet). It reads the destination IP address of each packet and, using its routing table, forwards the packet along the best path towards its destination. A home or office router usually also shares one Internet connection among several devices (NAT, DHCP, Wi-Fi).

questions.enonce_markdown:
(a) Storage devices are either optical or magnetic. List two examples of each of optical and magnetic. (2 marks)

(b) Describe one use of OCR to a secretary. (2 marks)

(c) Give ONE limitation of OCR. (1 mark)
questions.corrige_markdown:
**(a) Storage devices (2 marks).**

- *Optical:* CD-ROM / CD-R / CD-RW, DVD, Blu-ray disc.
- *Magnetic:* hard disk drive (HDD), magnetic tape, floppy disk.

(Any two of each. Optical devices store data as pits and lands read by a laser; magnetic devices store data as magnetised areas on a coated surface.)

**(b) Use of OCR to a secretary (2 marks).** OCR means *Optical Character Recognition*: software that analyses the scanned image of a printed or typed page and converts the shapes it recognises into editable text characters. A secretary can scan a printed letter, report or old document and convert it into a word-processor file that can be edited, corrected, searched and saved, instead of retyping the whole text. This saves a lot of time and reduces typing errors.

**(c) One limitation of OCR (1 mark).** OCR is not 100% accurate: poor-quality print, unusual fonts, stains or handwriting may be misread, so the converted text must be proofread and corrected.

questions.enonce_markdown:
Explain ONE application of computers in each of the following domains.

(a) Tourism. (2 marks)

(b) Banking. (2 marks)

(c) Marketing. (2 marks)
questions.corrige_markdown:
**(a) Tourism (2 marks).** *Online reservation and booking.* A computerised reservation system lets travel agents and tourists search and book flights, hotel rooms and tours over the Internet at any time, see prices and availability immediately and pay online, which avoids double booking and long journeys to an agency. (Other answers: virtual tours and websites that promote tourist sites; GPS navigation and e-tickets.)

**(b) Banking (2 marks).** *Automated Teller Machines (ATMs) and electronic funds transfer.* Customers use a card and a PIN to withdraw cash, check their balance or pay bills at any hour, and transfers between accounts are done instantly by computer (mobile banking, Internet banking), which reduces queues in the branch and the work of the cashiers. (Other answers: electronic clearing of cheques, computerised management of customer accounts.)

**(c) Marketing (2 marks).** *Online and e-mail advertising with a customer database.* Companies store customer details and buying habits in a database and use it to send targeted advertisements by e-mail, SMS and social media; the response of customers can be measured quickly and cheaply, so the company can reach many more potential buyers than with posters or radio alone. (Other answers: market research with questionnaires and spreadsheets; desktop publishing of brochures.)
